date_note: Date shown on ACER's own news item, which says the guidance is published 'today'.
exec: EU electricity operators and their ICT and security providers are asked, voluntarily, to submit annual counts of cyber threats, significant cyber-attacks and exploited zero-day vulnerabilities to ACER, in a window once every three years from 2027.
org: ACER (EU Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators)
plain: The EU energy regulators' agency updated its guidance on voluntary submission by power-sector companies of annual counts of cyber threats, significant cyber-attacks and exploited zero-day flaws, with a window once every three years from 2027.
summary: ACER published updated guidance under the EU Cybersecurity Network Code for voluntary submission of cybersecurity operational reliability indicators by electricity TSOs, DSOs, generators, NEMOs, organised markets, balancing responsible parties and critical ICT and managed security service providers. ACER says the first submission window, in 2027, will request data for 2026, then once every three years, covering annual counts of cyber threats, significant cyber-attacks and exploited zero-day vulnerabilities.
title: ACER updates guidance for EU electricity sector to report cybersecurity performance indicators

validation.note: Corroborated by a primary source and a second publisher: acer.europa.eu (ACER's own news item, 20 Nov) and sapo.pt (SAPO, 23 Nov) each state the update, the 2027 first collection covering 2026 and the three-yearly window. The guidance PDF itself was not read.

review.note: wording stronger than source: plain/exec said 'report yearly'; ACER says voluntary, annual counts, window once every three years from 2027. Fixed. Rest checked against ACER and SAPO.
